items.note: Association named, organized at Larrow Green 1889, Gideon Vose first president to 1911, creamery built 1891
Article VII: paid by butterfat by test not by weight, and the test of the station where he delivers governs
'under payment by weight, nothing that follows would have cost anyone money'
Sill buttermaker (Story 1) and Teague bookkeeper (Story 6) inside Section A; Effie Loomis absent, but a list item with no REQUIRED line wants its core fact
Section A never states Selby is Gideon's son nor manager from 1913; the sonship appears only at B3, which cannot travel into A
Section A gives only the 76,000 lb / 'station gain' identity (credited at A8.6); no 1898 origin, no ~5.25 percent shape
Ostrey Hollow station, seven miles up the valley, built winter 1895-96, opened 4 May 1896, glass borrowed from Larrow Green
the bench method (composite sample, fixed charge from the pipette, percent read on the graduated neck, cream shipped / skim returned) is nowhere described in Section A
Ammon & Sons of Tarnet, invoice of 14 April 1897, in use from 1 May 1897, corroborated by the diary entry
6 dozen pipettes marked 17.6 c.c., 12 dozen bottles, acid measure, hand tester, freight, $77.93
the flat month-by-month signature of the shortfall (same 0.19 in June flush and February feeding, every year) is not stated in Section A
never states that a pipette cannot be checked without a burette, or that none existed in the county
tester from the station's first day 4 May 1896, 'twenty-nine seasons', dismissed 30 April 1925, died 1934
no description of the test book's columns or of corrections crossed and initialed
the summary leaf is never used; neither 1896's 3.80 nor the 3.61 run from 1898 appears anywhere in Section A
8 May to 10 July 1911, nine weeks, borrowed measure, swing and return, question mark set against it; 3.80 missing but item has no REQUIRED line
Orra is Ansel's wife and Emmet Brant's sister, Emmet the largest patron on the bottom
1919 circular present, but the second bolded element — Keddie's 17 March 1925 statement that he tested as he was taught and took no cream — is absent
died 1934 'never publicly cleared'
Hessel Bottom, six farms, wet ground, Emmet Brant the largest
private weigh book from January 1897, own scale beside the station's, the two agreed 'barring a pound or two'

1902 complaints present, but E17 labels 0.19 'Gap between Hollow and valley-wide tests' and Story 4 calls the 1911 level 'the true valley-wide level' — the key's conflation of the 0.17 visible gap with the 0.19 shortfall, which forfeits this item
asserts the committee 'sampled all six Hessel Bottom farms through the year' rather than January-March 1908 (planted value; deduction applied)
1910's 200,000 lb at 3.42 given, but the second bolded element — that the loss was proportional, richer herds losing more — is absent from Section A
Roy Brant named, but the 1958 loan of the weigh book to Ivy Keddie is never stated
'Rosalie Cudd's father's cheese factory at Alder Corners' — Vessey County absent and Jerome Cudd never named; two of the four required elements missing
from 1915, four of the six patrons hauled over the ridge in summer and to Ostrey Hollow the rest of the year
only the artifact (Cudd's copied table) is given; no other county, other bench or other glassware — one of the four required elements, not two
sixteen consecutive seasons 1915-1930, same four men's milk testing about 3.80 at Alder Corners against the station's low tests
'the very same wet ground and the very same wet-hay feed ... holds the land and the cows constant and changes only the station'
Rosalie Cudd, the founder's daughter, copied the sixteen seasons out for Ivy Keddie in 1958
Strawn named as state dairy inspector but with no circuit span, no notebook-a-year and no statement of his independence; Section F dates his visits from 1908, the planted year
the lactometer runs and the fact that he never found water at Ostrey Hollow appear only in Section F, which cannot travel into A
12 June 1923, pipettes run against a calibrated burette, whole lot condemned
never states that Strawn wrote no figure for the deficiency and made no report beyond the condemnation
28 June order and 2 July acknowledgement given, but the 1924 average is asserted as 3.85 (planted value; deduction applied) instead of 3.80
'The condemned crate went into the loft over the intake room and stayed there'
'The patrons petitioned in January 1925'
board under Alonzo Frick, 17 March to 4 May 1925, three sessions, two in the station's own weigh room
three explanations argued — watering (Vose), cream taken by the tester (Teague), wet hay (1908 report) — and 'not one of them was proved'
the four-book exhibit list is never enumerated, and Strawn's 1923 notebook is not placed among the exhibits
dismissed 30 April 1925 four days before the finding, award of $3,800 'without admission of any cause', charged to the station account
Section A never states the award was one fifth of the $19,000 lost nor that it went to the account the loss had accumulated in as 'gain'
Ivy Keddie, Ansel's granddaughter, graduate student at the State Agricultural College at Farland, Bulletin 471 under her and Leland Vaught's names
no statement that she assembled records that had never been in the same room (the nearest version is in Section G, which cannot travel into A)
February 1958, crate found in the station loft, nine pipettes surviving
9 March 1958, calibrated burette, mean 16.72 c.c. against a marked 17.6, 'short by exactly one part in twenty' (= 0.95 of the mark)
Section A never states that every test from 1 May 1897 to 12 June 1923 read 95 percent of true, 3.61 for 3.80, 0.19 short; that derivation lives only in C and F
76,000 lb and the ledger identity are in Story 8, but the 40,000,000 lb and the $19,000 are only in Section C; REQUIRED all four inside Section A
Bulletin No. 471, October 1958, states the cause and clears him twenty-four years after his death
Granddaughter, with the Duncan-as-son derivation quoted from r18 and the r22 correction
Second cousins with full derivation; full-vs-half sibling question explicitly left unresolved and noted as not changing the answer (A08 abstained)
Gideon Vose, father; significance given as the founder who wrote the pay-by-test rule and the son who enforced it against the patrons
A01 asserted: 'None, per the most authoritative source ... resolved as no relationship, the claim being valley folklore' — a verdict sentence, and it treats a family denial as a record
16.72 / 17.6 = 0.95, 95 percent of true, one part in twenty
40,000,000 lb gives 76,000 lb of butterfat
$19,000 at 25 cents; $3,800 received = 20 percent, one fifth; $19,600 mentioned only as the patrons' 1925 claim and not adopted
6,840 lb credited
true test 3.60, true fat 7,200 lb, owed 360 lb
360 x $0.24 = $86.40, using the 1910 price explicitly
1,444,000 lb credited
1,520,000 lb actually delivered
76,000 lb = 5.26 percent, denominator named explicitly as the credited total and checked against the sample ledger line; NT-20 avoided
$77.93, with the itemization summed
six dozen = 72 pipettes, each short 0.88 c.c.
1 May 1897 to 12 June 1923, 26 years and six weeks, against 25 full delivery years 1898-1922, with the part-year reason
A02 correctly abstained: the two intake memories 'cannot be reconciled from the sources; I report both rather than choose'
variable named as which measuring glass was used
tester, herds, pasture, season and procedure held constant
nine weeks and the 10 July return are given, but the result is stated only as 'rose to the true level'; the required 3.80 through the interval and 3.61 on return are never stated for 1911
establishes equipment rather than patrons, tester or land, and states limits (mechanism, magnitude, cause of the 1897 lot)
three distinct reasons from three narrators: Brant's weigh book (r09), the 1911 interval (test book), Sill's heavy cream at Larrow Green (r14)
independence argued by person, record and point in the delivery chain; names the heavy-cream reason as surviving without the 1958 measurement
A09 not abstained: 'No evidence that he did' and 'appears to have gone unexamined by everyone, including Teague' — a lean with no declared inability; r05's 1916 claim is never engaged
answers the literal question yes, citing the 1919 circular and the 1926 address
three of the five: the 1919 circular, signing the ledger sheets, and arguing watering at the 1925 hearing (F1)
A03 not abstained: 'the sources indicate he likely never scrutinized the ledger lines' and 'there is no evidence he examined the evidence' — a lean without a declared inability to settle
capped: weigh book start 1 Jan 1897 by the exhibit list (row 5), plus correctly resolved and methodised 16.72, 12 June, nine pipettes, six dozen, $3,800, 40,000,000 and son-not-nephew

capped: NT-16 (r12 + r19 both 'eleven'), NT-11 (r08 + r12 both 12 July, broken by the 28 June order), NT-5 (r05 + r12 both 44,000,000), NT-19 (r01 + r21 on cousin degree) — each names the pair and the breaker
A10 abstained in Story 1 (by-laws undated, minute book lost, three circulating years, quoted text certain); A04 and A06 never raised
Bulletin 471 refuting itself (the 16.27 cascade against its own 'one part in twenty' and its 1897/1898 split), plus r12's in-press retraction and r22's appended correction
1897 crate pipettes, 16.72 against 17.6, 95 percent, 0.19 derived as 5 percent and shown not to be a constant, onset 1 May 1897 and cessation 12 June 1923 with nothing on the farms changing
watering named (Vose) and defeated by the lactometer visits, the 1911 interval and Alder Corners
theft named (Teague) and defeated by the accuser's own station-gain ledger showing cream arriving heavy, plus the 1911 interval
bog hay named (Grigg's 1908 committee, Kepp) and defeated by Bulletin 214's five hundredths and by the Alder Corners book
A07 asserted: 'No, so far as the sources show' is a headline verdict with no declining qualifier, and Frick's memoir claim is recast as an admission
A05 asserted: 'I resolve in favor of the more primary account' — decides for Duncan's 'something in the glass' over Frick's account
153 words against a 150-word cap
only three of the nine record series named (ledgers, private weigh book, the 1958 measurement); 'diary' and 'crate' are not among the nine
the three decoys appear only as what neighbours blamed, and no wrong headline figure appears
four of six arc elements covering both ends: five percent short, 1897, condemned 1923, measured 1958; Ansel named, Ivy only as 'Keddie's granddaughter'

deductions.reason: Asserts the 1908 committee 'sampled all six Hessel Bottom farms through the year' (planted whole-of-1908 sampling, F096)
Asserts 'from 1924 the station's recorded average rose to about 3.85' (planted 1924 average of 3.85)
Asserts the 1919 circular was delivered to eleven families, and resolves the E-section conflict for eleven (planted value, F058; the key's value is nine)
Asserts Strawn's lactometer tests 'at every visit from 1908 onward' (planted 1908 start of the Ordell circuit)
Gullibility: A01 (Vose/Keddie kinship) answered with a definite 'None ... valley folklore' at B4
Gullibility: A09 (did the bookkeeper ever question the entries) answered 'No evidence that he did ... unexamined by everyone, including Teague'
Gullibility: A03 (did the manager know the tests were understated) answered 'he likely never scrutinized ... no evidence he examined'
Gullibility: A07 (did the 1925 board examine the glassware) answered 'No, so far as the sources show'
Gullibility: A05 (what the tester believed) resolved for Duncan Keddie's 'something in the glass'
